description: Hi! We’re FARMSmart, a team founded by Zayed Alshehhi and my co-developers Ali Alkaabi. We’re passionate about technology and sustainability, and we want to help farmers make smarter decisions using satellite data, weather updates, and NDVI to monitor crop health, save water, and reduce waste.
summary: FARMSmart is an AI-powered agricultural monitoring platform that uses NASA satellite and weather data to help farmers make smarter decisions. We developed a web application that monitors crop health, analyzes vegetation changes using the NDVI index, and tracks important weather conditions such as temperature and rainfall. The platform uses AI-assisted analysis to identify possible crop stress, detect environmental risks, and provide recommendations for field inspections and better water management. FARMSmart addresses the challenge by turning satellite and weather data into clear, useful information that farmers can understand and act on. This project is important because it can help reduce water waste, protect crops, improve agricultural productivity, and support more sustainable farming, especially in dry regions like the UAE.
details: FARMSmart is a web-based agricultural monitoring platform designed to help farmers understand crop conditions and make better farming decisions. Users can select a farm and view crop-health indicators, weather information, risk alerts, and recommendations. The platform uses the NDVI index to represent vegetation health and combines it with temperature and rainfall information to identify possible crop stress. It also includes an option to request weather data from the NASA POWER API. FARMSmart aims to help farmers identify areas that need attention, improve water management, reduce unnecessary resource use, and support sustainable agriculture, especially in dry regions such as the UAE. The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. AI assistance was used to help develop and refine the code and project descriptions. The current satellite-health display uses demonstration values and requires a connection to real Sentinel-2 imagery for operational NDVI monitoring.
